title: Weakly contractible covers within the affine ind-etale basis
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the fixed small pro-etale site and universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Give $S_{\mathrm{app}}=\mathcal B_S$, the full subcategory of affine schemes ind-etale over $S$, its induced coverings [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Every object $U$ of $S_{\mathrm{app}}$ has a covering family $\{V_j\to U\}$ in $S_{\mathrm{app}}$ such that each $V_j$ is weakly contractible in this same site. Here weakly contractible means that every epimorphism $P\to Q$ of sheaves of sets on $S_{\mathrm{app}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] induces a surjection $P(V_j)\to Q(V_j)$; an epimorphism is a right-cancellable morphism. In particular the covering objects are themselves affine and ind-etale over $S$, not merely objects of the full pro-etale site.

source.place: Tag 0990, lemma-proetale-enough-w-contractible, clause for affine S and S_app; weak contractibility: sites.tex Tags 090L and 090K condition (2)

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Choose an infinite cardinal $\kappa\geq |A|$ in the object universe. The bounded ring-extension lemma supplies a faithfully flat ind-etale $A\to D$, with $|D|\leq\kappa^{2^{2^{2^\kappa}}}$, such that every faithfully flat weakly etale map out of $D$ has a retraction, and $V=\operatorname{Spec}D\to U$ is a singleton pro-etale covering. The ind-etale composition clause makes $V\to U\to S$ ind-etale, since $U\to S$ is ind-etale by the basis definition. Thus $V$ is affine and lies in $\mathcal B_S$. The displayed cardinal is still in the Grothendieck object universe, which is closed under power sets and function sets; after replacing by its skeleton representative, $V$ remains an allowed object. The induced-covering definition then makes $\{V\to U\}$ a covering in $S_{\mathrm{app}}$.

Fix an epimorphism $\varphi:P\to Q$ of sheaves of sets on $S_{\mathrm{app}}$ and $s\in Q(V)$. Apply the site-general epimorphism/local-surjectivity equivalence to this site, obtaining a covering $\{f_i:T_i\to V\}_{i\in I}$ and $t_i\in P(T_i)$ with $\varphi(t_i)=s|_{T_i}$. By the induced-covering definition this is also a pro-etale covering of schemes. The retraction property of $D$ from step 1 is precisely the hypothesis of the covering-section lemma. It supplies $\sigma:V\to C=\coprod_i T_i$ with $p\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_V$, where $p$ restricts to $f_i$ on the $i$th component. Here $C$ is only a scheme; it is not asserted to be an object of the affine basis.

source.place: Tag 098H (lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible), (3) implies (2), local lifting; Tag 098F (lemma-w-contractible-proetale-cover), covering section; Sites Tags 00WM and 00WN

proof.text: The coproduct lemma says its component images are pairwise disjoint clopen subsets covering $C$. Their inverse images $O_i=\sigma^{-1}(T_i)$ therefore form a disjoint open covering of $V$. The restriction $\sigma_i:O_i\to T_i$ has $f_i\circ\sigma_i:O_i\to V$ equal to the open inclusion. Each $O_i$ is an object of the full small pro-etale site: its inclusion in $V$ is an open immersion, hence etale and flat; its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence flat on local rings, so it is weakly etale. Composition with $V\to S$ is weakly etale by composition stability. Opens do not enlarge the universe. The family $\{O_i\to V\}$ is a pro-etale covering: for an affine test open $W\subseteq V$, take affine neighborhoods subordinate to the open covering $(W\cap O_i)_i$; quasi-compactness of the affine $W$ gives finitely many of these affine opens with union $W$, exactly the required witnesses in the covering definition. No $O_i$ is assumed affine or ind-etale.

source.place: Tag 098F, inverse images of the coproduct components; Tag 098H, disjoint open covering in (3) implies (2); Tag 0989, definition-fpqc-covering

proof.text: Apply the basis-refinement clause to the full-site covering $\{O_i\to V\}$ of the basis object $V$. Obtain a finite covering $\{a_k:W_k\to V\}_{k\in K}$ with every $W_k\in\mathcal B_S$, and refinement maps $b_k:W_k\to O_{i(k)}$ such that $a_k$ is the inclusion of $O_{i(k)}$ composed with $b_k$. Put $h_k=\sigma_{i(k)}\circ b_k:W_k\to T_{i(k)}$. Then $f_{i(k)}\circ h_k=a_k$. The maps $h_k$ are $S$-morphisms between basis objects, hence are morphisms in the full subcategory $S_{\mathrm{app}}$. Thus $u_k=P(h_k)(t_{i(k)})$ is defined entirely on this site, and naturality gives $\varphi(u_k)=Q(a_k)(s)$.

source.place: Tag 0990, affine S_app clause, with the refinement of Tag 098H open-and-closed lifts by Tag 098X (lemma-affine-alternative)

proof.text: The same basis lemma puts $W_k\times_V W_l$ in the basis. If $i(k)\ne i(l)$, this fibre product is empty because $O_{i(k)}$ and $O_{i(l)}$ are disjoint. The empty scheme belongs to the basis (its ring is the zero ring, a principal localization at zero), and its empty covering makes the sheaf equalizer the map to an empty product, so $P(\varnothing)=Q(\varnothing)=\{*\}$ up to the unique bijection. In particular the two restrictions on an empty overlap coincide. If $i(k)=i(l)=i$, the two maps from the fibre product into $T_i$ agree: both are the factorization into the $i$th open component of $\sigma\circ a_k\circ\operatorname{pr}_k=\sigma\circ a_l\circ\operatorname{pr}_l$. Since that component is an open subscheme, this factorization is unique. Hence the two restrictions of $u_k,u_l$ agree, both being the pullback of $t_i$ along that map. The sheaf equalizer axiom glues the $u_k$ to $u\in P(V)$. Naturality and the equalizer injectivity for $Q$ give $\varphi(u)=s$, since they have identical restrictions on the covering. Thus $V$ is weakly contractible on $S_{\mathrm{app}}$. This applies to every $U$ by step 1, including the empty $U$: an empty basis refinement gives the unique glued section. The argument used no extension of $P$ or $Q$ to the full site.
